newsitem.title: CANADA: APEC officials set outline for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: APEC officials set outline for trade talks.

text.p: Senior trade officials from Asian-Pacific countries succeeded in setting up a process to target sectors for free trade in the region, a Canadian official said on Thursday after a three-day meeting.

"I think it was very successful," Len Edwards, a senior Canadian trade official who chaired the meeting, told Reuters by telephone from Quebec City, where the meeting occurred. "We had high hopes and the end, we were rewarded."

Canada is hosting this year's meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. Trade ministers from the group's 18 countries met in Montreal last weekend to discuss trade issues ahead of a summit in Vancouver in November.
APEC aims to foster free trade among its member countries.
The officials could now return to their countries with a framework to isolate sectors for liberalisation, Edwards said.
Every country that wished to propose a sector for liberalisation would have until mid-July to put together a proposal, he said.

There have been at least 15 suggestions for liberalisation that arose from last week's trade ministers' meeting. Canada backs free trade in environmental products and services, while the United States would likely put together a proposal to liberalise markets in chemicals, he said.
Australia would likely put forward a package on energy and Thailand will probably propose processed foods, he added.
Senior officials will meet again at the end of August in St. John's, Newfoundland, to take the proposals to the next step.
Officials have said they hope to have two or three sectors on the table at the Vancouver summit.
